To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of farmers in the sample self-reported that they had adopted coping strategies in response to climate changes, but that the adoption was limited to a few coping strategies and was not evenly distributed across the study population.

farmers in the coastal region of Bangladesh are adopting a variety of coping strategies to adapt to climate change and environmental degradation, and that farmers’ age, education, and family size were found to be significantly related to the adoption of coping strategies.

(1) a majority of farmers in coastal Bangladesh self-identify as having engaged in adaptation behavior, (2) irrigation is the most commonly used coping mechanism, (3) education and family income are positively correlated with the adoption of adaptive measures, (4) the lack of water, cultivable land, unpredictable weather are the most commonly reported obstacles to adaptation, and (5) the majority of farmers in the sample perceive that climate change is already having an effect on their livelihoods
